message.content:
In /bench/repo, research the store layer:
1. Find the main driver interface that all database backends implement - look for interface definitions in store/ directory
2. Find the PostgreSQL driver struct and its file
3. Find ALL three database driver implementations and their entry files
4. Find the factory function that selects between drivers at startup
5. Find the store.Memo struct definition and its file
6. Find structs that map to tables: user, attachment, reaction
7. Find the Store.CreateMemo method and where it's defined
8. Find the Store.GetUser method and all its call sites across the entire codebase
9. Find what happens when DeleteMemo runs - what other records are deleted
10. Look at the memo_relation table or similar linking table
11. Find the SQL migration files - what dialects are supported (look in store/db/ or similar)
12. Find the latest/complete SQLite schema file

Search thoroughly across all store/ files. Read the key files. Report everything.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

3	import (
4		"sync"
5		"time"
6	
7		"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/profile"
8		storepb "github.com/usememos/memos/proto/gen/store"
9		"github.com/usememos/memos/store/cache"
10	)
11	
12	// Store provides database access to all raw objects.
13	type Store struct {
14		profile *profile.Profile
15		driver  Driver
16	
17		userCreateMu sync.Mutex
18		authConfigMu sync.Mutex
19	
20		deploymentConfigMu sync.RWMutex
21		deploymentConfig   *deploymentConfiguration
22	
23		// Cache settings
24		cacheConfig cache.Config
25	
26		// Caches
27		instanceSettingCache *cache.Cache // cache for instance settings
28		userCache            *cache.Cache // cache for users
29		userSettingCache     *cache.Cache // cache for user settings
30	}
31	
32	type deploymentConfiguration struct {
33		identityProviders map[string]*storepb.IdentityProvider
34		instanceSettings  map[storepb.InstanceSettingKey]*storepb.InstanceSetting
35	}
36	
37	// New creates a new instance of Store.
38	func New(driver Driver, profile *profile.Profile) *Store {
39		// Default cache settings
40		cacheConfig := cache.Config{
41			DefaultTTL:      10 * time.Minute,
42			CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,
43			MaxItems:        1000,
44			OnEviction:      nil,
45		}
46	
47		store := &Store{
48			driver:               driver,
49			profile:              profile,
50			cacheConfig:          cacheConfig,
51			instanceSettingCache: cache.New(cacheConfig),
52			userCache:            cache.New(cacheConfig),
53			userSettingCache:     cache.New(cacheConfig),
54			deploymentConfig: &deploymentConfiguration{
55				identityProviders: map[string]*storepb.IdentityProvider{},
56				instanceSettings:  map[storepb.InstanceSettingKey]*storepb.InstanceSetting{},
57			},
58		}
59	
60		return store
61	}
62	
63	func (s *Store) GetDriver() Driver {
64		return s.driver
65	}
66	
67	// GetDataDir returns the store data directory.
68	func (s *Store) GetDataDir() string {
69		return s.profile.Data
70	}
71	
72	func (s *Store) Close() error {
73		// Stop all cache cleanup goroutines
74		s.instanceSettingCache.Close()
75		s.userCache.Close()
76		s.userSettingCache.Close()
77	
78		return s.driver.Close()
79	}

21	// NewDB opens a database specified by its database driver name and a
22	// driver-specific data source name, usually consisting of at least a
23	// database name and connection information.
24	func NewDB(profile *profile.Profile) (store.Driver, error) {
25		// Ensure a DSN is set before attempting to open the database.
26		if profile.DSN == "" {
27			return nil, errors.New("dsn required")
28		}
29	
30		if err := ensureUnicodeLowerRegistered(); err != nil {
31			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to register sqlite unicode lower function")
32		}
33	
34		if err := ensureRegexpRegistered(); err != nil {
35			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to register sqlite regexp function")
36		}
37	
38		// Connect to the database with some sane settings:
39		// - No shared-cache: it's obsolete; WAL journal mode is a better solution.
40		// - No foreign key constraints: it's currently disabled by default, but it's a
41		// good practice to be explicit and prevent future surprises on SQLite upgrades.
42		// - Journal mode set to WAL: it's the recommended journal mode for most applications
43		// as it prevents locking issues.
44		// - mmap size set to 0: it disables memory mapping, which can cause OOM errors on some systems.
45		//
46		// Notes:
47		// - When using the `modernc.org/sqlite` driver, each pragma must be prefixed with `_pragma=`.
48		//
49		// References:
50		// - https://pkg.go.dev/modernc.org/sqlite#Driver.Open
51		// - https://www.sqlite.org/sharedcache.html
52		// - https://www.sqlite.org/pragma.html
53		sqliteDB, err := sql.Open("sqlite", profile.DSN+"?_pragma=foreign_keys(0)&_pragma=busy_timeout(10000)&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)&_pragma=mmap_size(0)")
54		if err != nil {
55			return nil, errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to open db with dsn: %s", profile.DSN)
56		}
57	
58		driver := DB{db: sqliteDB, profile: profile}
59	
60		return &driver, nil
61	}

73		var exists bool
74		err := d.db.QueryRowContext(ctx, "SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='memo')").Scan(&exists)
75		if err != nil {

83		var pageCount, pageSize int64
84		if err := d.db.QueryRowContext(ctx, "PRAGMA page_count").Scan(&pageCount); err != nil {
85			return -1, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read page_count")

28	// 2. checkMinimumUpgradeVersion: Verify installation can be upgraded (reject pre-0.22 installations)
29	// 3. Migrate (prod mode): Apply incremental migrations from current to target version

40	// - Naming: NN is zero-padded patch number, description is human-readable
41	// - Ordering: Files sorted lexicographically and applied in order

## Store Layer Research Report

### 1. Main Driver Interface

**File:** `/bench/repo/store/driver.go`

The `Driver` interface (lines 10-86) is the central contract that all database backends must implement. It defines methods for every data model:

- `GetDB() *sql.DB`, `Close() error`, `IsInitialized()`, `GetDatabaseSize()`
- CRUD for: Attachment, Memo, MemoRelation, InstanceSetting, User, UserSetting, IdentityProvider, Inbox, Reaction, MemoShare, UserIdentity

### 2. PostgreSQL Driver Struct

**File:** `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/postgres.go`

```go
type DB struct {
    db      *sql.DB
    profile *profile.Profile
}
```

Constructor is `func NewDB(profile *profile.Profile) (store.Driver, error)` (line 21). It uses the `github.com/lib/pq` driver.

### 3. All Three Database Driver Implementations

| Driver     | Entry File                                       | Struct                                              |
|------------|--------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| **SQLite** | `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go`          | `type DB struct { db *sql.DB; profile *profile.Profile }` |
| **PostgreSQL** | `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/postgres.go`  | `type DB struct { db *sql.DB; profile *profile.Profile }` |
| **MySQL**  | `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/mysql.go`             | `type DB struct { db *sql.DB; profile *profile.Profile; config *mysql.Config }` |

Each driver directory mirrors the same set of files (memo.go, user.go, attachment.go, reaction.go, etc.) implementing the `store.Driver` interface.

### 4. Factory Function

**File:** `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go`

```go
func NewDBDriver(profile *profile.Profile) (store.Driver, error) {
    switch profile.Driver {
    case "sqlite":
        driver, err = sqlite.NewDB(profile)
    case "mysql":
        driver, err = mysql.NewDB(profile)
    case "postgres":
        driver, err = postgres.NewDB(profile)
    default:
        return nil, errors.New("unknown db driver")
    }
}
```

This is the factory that selects the database backend at startup based on `profile.Driver`.

### 5. Store.Memo Struct

**File:** `/bench/repo/store/memo.go` (lines 35-55)

```go
type Memo struct {
    ID         int32
    UID        string
    RowStatus  RowStatus
    CreatorID  int32
    CreatedTs  int64
    UpdatedTs  int64
    Content    string
    Visibility Visibility
    Pinned     bool
    Payload    *storepb.MemoPayload
    ParentUID  *string
}
```

### 6. Structs Mapping to Tables

**User** -- `/bench/repo/store/user.go` (lines 29-45):
```go
type User struct {
    ID, RowStatus, CreatedTs, UpdatedTs,
    Username, Role, Email, Nickname, PasswordHash, AvatarURL, Description
}
```

**Attachment** -- `/bench/repo/store/attachment.go` (lines 17-41):
```go
type Attachment struct {
    ID, UID, CreatorID, CreatedTs, UpdatedTs,
    Filename, Blob, Type, Size, StorageType, Reference, Payload,
    MemoID, MemoUID
}
```

**Reaction** -- `/bench/repo/store/reaction.go` (lines 8-14):
```go
type Reaction struct {
    ID, CreatedTs, CreatorID, ContentID, ReactionType
}
```

### 7. Store.CreateMemo Method

**File:** `/bench/repo/store/memo.go` (lines 109-114)

```go
func (s *Store) CreateMemo(ctx context.Context, create *Memo) (*Memo, error) {
    if !base.UIDMatcher.MatchString(create.UID) {
        return nil, errors.New("invalid uid")
    }
    return s.driver.CreateMemo(ctx, create)
}
```

It validates the UID format then delegates to the driver.

### 8. Store.GetUser Method and All Call Sites

**Definition:** `/bench/repo/store/user.go` (line 148)

**Call sites across the entire codebase** (excluding test files and generated protobuf stubs):

| File | Line | Context |
|------|------|---------|
| `/bench/repo/server/auth/authenticator.go` | 87 | Authenticating a user by ID from session |
| `/bench/repo/server/auth/authenticator.go` | 159 | Validating JWT claims user ID |
| `/bench/repo/server/notification/email.go` | 60 | Looking up inbox receiver for email notification |
| `/bench/repo/server/notification/email.go` | 68 | Looking up inbox sender for email notification |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go` | 126 | Finding user for RSS feed generation |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` | 716 | Looking up user by username for file serving |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_session.go` | 251 | Finding user during session-based sign-in |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service.go` | 56 | Finding user during authentication |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go` | 90 | Finding winner user during SSO conflict resolution |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go` | 161 | Finding user by identity during SSO |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/connect_services.go` | 114-115 | Connect gateway delegating to APIV1Service.GetUser |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/instance_service.go` | 334 | Looking up user in instance service |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service.go` | 171 | The gRPC GetUser API endpoint |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_resource_name.go` | 54 | Resolving user resource name by username |
| `/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go` | 135 | Looking up user when processing PAT hash results |
| `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user.go` | 77, 188 | MySQL driver internal: UpdateUser re-reads the user; also has its own GetUser helper |

### 9. What Happens When DeleteMemo Runs

**File:** `/bench/repo/store/memo.go` (lines 140-159)

The `DeleteMemo` method performs a cascading cleanup in this order:

1. **Delete memo_relation records** where this memo is the **source** (`MemoID`).
2. **Delete memo_relation records** where this memo is the **target** (`RelatedMemoID`).
3. **List all attachments** linked to this memo.
4. **Delete each attachment** individually (which also deletes the attachment's physical storage -- local file or S3 object -- and derived caches like thumbnails).
5. **Delete the memo row itself** via `s.driver.DeleteMemo()`.

Note: `memo_share` has a SQL-level `ON DELETE CASCADE` foreign key on `memo_id`, so those rows are cleaned up automatically by the database when the memo row is deleted.

### 10. Memo Relation Table / Linking Table

**Struct file:** `/bench/repo/store/memo_relation.go`

The `MemoRelation` struct maps to the `memo_relation` table:

```go
type MemoRelation struct {
    MemoID        int32
    RelatedMemoID int32
    Type          MemoRelationType  // "REFERENCE" or "COMMENT"
}
```

The table has a composite unique key on `(memo_id, related_memo_id, type)`. It supports two relation types:
- `REFERENCE` -- one memo references another
- `COMMENT` -- one memo is a comment on another

There is also a **`memo_share`** linking table (`/bench/repo/store/memo_share.go`) for share-link grants:
```go
type MemoShare struct {
    ID, UID, MemoID, CreatorID, CreatedTs int32/int64
    ExpiresTs *int64  // nil = never expires
}
```

### 11. SQL Migration Files and Supported Dialects

**Three dialects are supported**, each with its own migration directory:

| Dialect | Migration Directory | Version Range |
|---------|-------------------|---------------|
| **SQLite** | `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/` | 0.2 through 0.30 (plus 0.10-0.28) |
| **PostgreSQL** | `/bench/repo/store/migration/postgres/` | 0.19 through 0.30 |
| **MySQL** | `/bench/repo/store/migration/mysql/` | 0.17 through 0.30 |

Each dialect has a `LATEST.sql` file for fresh installations plus versioned subdirectories containing incremental migration scripts. Migration file naming follows the pattern `NN__description.sql` (e.g., `00__memo.sql`, `01__memo_pinned.sql`).

The migration system is managed by `/bench/repo/store/migrator.go`, which embeds the migration files via `//go:embed migration`. For new installations, it applies `LATEST.sql` directly; for upgrades, it applies incremental migrations from the current version forward.

### 12. Latest/Complete SQLite Schema

**File:** `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql`

The complete SQLite schema defines these tables:

| Table | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `system_setting` | Key-value instance settings (name, value, description) |
| `user` | User accounts (id, username, role, email, nickname, password_hash, avatar_url, description, row_status, timestamps) |
| `user_setting` | Per-user settings (user_id, key, value) |
| `memo` | Memos/notes (id, uid, creator_id, content, visibility, pinned, payload, row_status, timestamps) |
| `memo_relation` | Memo-to-memo links (memo_id, related_memo_id, type) with unique constraint on all three |
| `attachment` | File attachments (id, uid, creator_id, filename, blob, type, size, memo_id, storage_type, reference, payload) |
| `idp` | Identity providers (id, uid, name, type, identifier_filter, config) |
| `inbox` | Notification inbox (id, sender_id, receiver_id, status, message) |
| `reaction` | Emoji reactions (id, creator_id, content_id, reaction_type) with unique on (creator_id, content_id, reaction_type) |
| `memo_share` | Share-link grants (id, uid, memo_id, creator_id, expires_ts) with FK cascade on memo(id) |
| `user_identity` | External identity bindings (id, user_id, provider, extern_uid) with unique on (provider, extern_uid) and (user_id, provider) |
